kicker: Telecom · EBITDA growth vs ARPU, Q2 FY27
title: Mobile EBITDA grew 14–18% without a new tariff hike
dek: Jio's ARPU (average revenue per user a month) rose only 3.5% in a year, yet the three mobile operators grew Q2 EBITDA 14–18%. On its Q2 call Jio said no tariff decision has been taken, about 2.5 years after the last hike.

chart.title: EBITDA growth, Q2 FY27 vs Q2 FY26
chart.sub: filed results; Jio from its Q2 call (consolidated) · label shows revenue growth · *Indus +5.2% excluding a one-off in the base

hero.label: Jio's ARPU growth in a year
hero.note: ₹211.4 → ₹218.8 a month, Q2 FY26 to Q2 FY27: price did little of the work

read: Profit growth is coming from mix, upgrades and cost, not price: EBITDA outgrew revenue at five of six, so any tariff hike would land on already-widening margins.
sources: Vantage analysis of Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE and Q2 FY27 earnings calls
notes: EBITDA and revenue growth are year on year from filed Q2 FY27 results (consolidated; Hexacom and TTML standalone), except Jio Platforms, whose filing in our data is the standalone holding company, so its consolidated growth (revenue +11.4%, EBITDA +16.6%) and ARPU are as stated on its Q2 call. Airtel's figures are group-wide and include Africa. We set out to compare ARPU across operators, but the data does not allow it: Airtel's Q2 call summary repeats its Q1 call (same revenue and ARPU of ₹264), Bharti Hexacom's Q2 entry covers Q4 FY26, and Vodafone Idea has neither a Q2 call nor Q2 results in our data, so only Jio's ARPU (₹211.4 → ₹218.8, +3.5%) is a clean Q2 figure; Vodafone Idea is left out. Indus Towers' reported EBITDA growth is held down by a roughly ₹2 bn one-off write-back in Q2 FY26; it says growth was +5.2% excluding it. Hook: Jio's Q2 call, where management said there is no tariff decision yet, about 2.5 years after the last hike, and that ARPU is not the only lever (Airtel's tariff comments are not used because its Q2 summary duplicates Q1). A web search on 21 Nov 2026 found reports speculating on a hike but no announced tariff change, so none is assumed here.
